messages:
Maria Nguyen: hey @Sara (Legal) — I'm kicking off intake for a community model we want to evaluate internally: 'Concordia-6B'. License text looks messy (NC + ND-ish). Need quick guidance on whether we can: 1) run internal evals, 2) quantize for latency tests, 3) host in Dedicated/Hosted/Private. Short checklist attached below.

Sara (Legal): paste the excerpt when you have it and flag any permalink to their repo/TOS.

Maria Nguyen: sure, excerpt from model-card/LICENSE.txt: 
```
"This model is provided under the Concordia Research License v1.0. Use is permitted for non-commercial research and evaluation only. No derivative works or redistribution of model weights or modified checkpoints is allowed without prior written permission. Commercial deployment or offering of the model (including hosted APIs) is prohibited."
```
Link: https://huggingface.co/concordia/concordia-6b (model card)

Sara (Legal): quick read: two red flags — NC (non-commercial) and ND (no derivatives/redistribution). NC typically prevents us from offering the model via our hosted API or in any paid product. ND is trickier: it likely prohibits creating modified weights (quantized/statically-compiled variants) or distributing checkpoints. We need to confirm whether quantization for internal eval counts as a "derivative" under their license.

Ajay Rao: from an infra/tech side — if ND forbids weight modification, that effectively blocks us from: shipping quantized weights, publishing optimized artifacts, or applying model surgery. Running ephemeral quantized inference locally for internal evals might be tolerated if we do not export/distribute the resulting weights. But that’s a legal call. For Dedicated: if the customer brings their own weights and we just run them, product-wise that's plausible (we're not redistributing). Hosted API is a no-go unless we get redistribution/commercial rights.

Cheng Wu: also flag fine-tuning: ND probably means no fine-tuning because that creates a derivative model. Even small adapter-based tuning could be considered a derivative. We should presume no fine-tune until legal confirms.

Sam Keller: operational question — can we run a one-off isolated quant smoke in a private lab (air-gapped) with the weights for perf numbers and then delete everything? We need to know whether bench numbers from that run can be quoted internally or in public docs.

Sara (Legal): internal benching that stays internal and is not incorporated into a commercial product is more defensible, but I want explicit answers about two things: (a) whether quantization equals "derivative work" under their license, (b) whether internal benchmarking counts as commercial use for them. I’ll request clarification from the model authors; sometimes maintainers provide a research-only license but will grant a limited hosting/quantization waiver on request.

Liz Brooks: product question — we have a pilot request from a non-paying partner to test latency. If legal says NC blocks "commercial use", would that partner pilot be allowed as long as it's marked "research" and no SLA? We need a simple rule for the pilot gating doc.

Sara (Legal): generally treat any partner-facing pilot that exercises product functionality as commercial unless the partner is explicitly in a research collaboration with an MOU. Recommend: treat pilot as commercial by default. If the partner signs a research-only agreement, we can proceed; otherwise ask for permission from rights holder.

Maria Nguyen: action items I propose: 
1) Legal: reach out to model authors/maintainers to request written clarification + quantization/hosting waiver. (Sara)
2) Eng-ML: run an internal, ephemeral quant smoke in an air-gapped environment, store logs only, delete artifacts after testing. Do not publish artifacts. (Ajay/Cheng)
3) Product: treat partner pilots as commercial by default; require research MOU to proceed without waiver. (Liz)
4) Ops/Sales: if customer wants Dedicated with their own weights, confirm flow that avoids us redistributing weights. (Sam)
5) Onboard-bot: record intake and priority for follow-up. (onboard-bot)

onboard-bot: Model intake recorded: concordia-6b submitted_by=Maria Nguyen priority=medium tags=[license-review, export-check, quant-triage] ticket=#ml-intake-4678

Ajay Rao: noted — I’ll create an isolated VM with ephemeral storage and run a single 8-bit quant smoke. Will not checkpoint or commit quantized weights to any repo. ETA: EOD tomorrow.

Cheng Wu: I’ll prepare eval prompts and perf harness. Will redact any dataset sources that might be regulated.

Sara (Legal): I’ve emailed the maintainers with two questions (quantization as derivative? permission to host in private deployments with customer-supplied weights?). Will post updates in this thread.

Sam Keller: tagging infra for export control scan — @infra-team please confirm whether model originates in a jurisdiction with export restrictions.

Liz Brooks: thanks all. If legal gives a waiver, we should add explicit license clauses to the model gate doc so onboarders know what is allowed.

Maria Nguyen: treat this as blocked-on-legal for hosted/dedicated/public hosting. We can proceed with internal bench smoke under constraints. Keeping thread short — will update once Sara replies. :thumbsup:
